# implement.py parent ignores the do-not-delegate tag when selecting the next child

relocated-from:AH-0MUWGZ7UH007NBT4 (AI_Hell worklog), moved to this repo because `implement.py` is agent-infrastructure code owned by SorraAgents (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`).

discovered-from:AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J

## Problem statement

`implement.py parent` selects the next startable child purely from status, dependency order and `sortIndex`, so a child tagged `do-not-delegate` is claimed and started on every dispatch — the epic then livelocks on the one child that must not be automated, and its genuinely startable siblings are never reached.

## Users

- **Automated dispatchers** (herdr downtime worker running `implement.py parent <epic>` / `drive <epic>` unattended):
  *As the dispatcher, when the lowest-sorting remaining child is `do-not-delegate`, I want it reported as guarded and skipped so the next genuinely startable sibling runs — or a clean "no startable child" stop — instead of a claim/worktree churn cycle every cycle.*
- **Operators driving an epic manually:**
  *As an operator, I want the parent report to tell me which child is guarded and why nothing started, so I do not have to abort a wrongly-claimed child before the real work can proceed.*
- **Maintainers:**
  *As a maintainer, I want the guard covered by a regression test with the exact shape that broke (guarded child lowest `sortIndex`, open startable siblings), so the selection rule cannot silently regress.*

## Observed failure

AI_Hell epic `AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J`: child **Evaluate switching to runtime generation when ToneForge is Runtime-ready (AH-0MUTVQDH2008DEF6)** carries the `do-not-delegate` tag and must stay unstarted until the external item **Make ToneForge Runtime-aware (browser-compatible playback) (TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0)** is terminal. `implement.py parent` started it anyway, on every re-run, leaving the three startable siblings (Thruster hum Tone.js shim, Update audio documentation, Pin ToneForge and bundle hygiene) unreached until an operator aborted the guarded child manually. The previous session recorded the same gap in a comment on 2026-10-05T21:17Z.

## Existing state (verified in this checkout)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `_classify_child()` (line ~872) returns only `skip-terminal` / `skip-in-progress` / `implement` — `tags` are never consulted anywhere in the module (`grep do-not-delegate` → zero hits in the repo).
- The live selection path is the `phase_parent()` child loop (line ~5830); `_next_child_to_implement()` (line ~963) is **not called by production code** — only by tests. A fix limited to `_next_child_to_implement()` would not change behaviour.
- `wl_show_children()` (line ~473) already returns each child's `tags` array from `wl show <id> --children --json` (verified against live data) — honouring the tag needs **no** extra `wl` subprocess and no schema change.
- The current waiting branch (line ~5935) reports only `blocked_children` and the message "blocked by non-terminal siblings or another agent holds them" — a guarded child would be mis-described by it.
- `phase_drive()` (line ~6656) consumes `parent.next_child` and stops when it is absent, passing `blocked_children` through.
- `wl` itself already treats `do-not-delegate` as a guard rail (`worklog` `delegate-helper.js`): it refuses to hand such an item to an automated agent unless `--force`. `implement.py` selecting that child for an automated implement session is the same delegation, so the semantics align. 33 items in this store currently carry the tag.

## Desired change

Treat a `do-not-delegate`-tagged child as **not startable by automatic parent recursion**, report it distinctly, and leave explicit invocation as the documented override.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Guarded classification.** A child whose `tags` contain `do-not-delegate` classifies as a dedicated guarded action (e.g. `skip-do-not-delegate`) via `_classify_child()`, matched case- and whitespace-insensitively and safe against a missing/`None` `tags` field; `_next_child_to_implement()` skips it in the same way it skips terminal children.
- [ ] **AC2 — Parent never starts a guarded child.** `phase_parent()` neither claims (`status=in_progress`) nor creates a worktree for a guarded child. It records `action: "skipped-do-not-delegate"` in `children_processed`, lists the ids in a `guarded_children` report field, and still starts the next startable sibling in dependency/`sortIndex` order.
- [ ] **AC3 — No premature advance, distinct waiting report.** When the only non-terminal children left are guarded, the parent is **not** advanced to `completed`/`in_review`, no `next_child` is reported, and the message names the guarded children and the tag (not the dependency-blocked wording). Re-running the phase is idempotent: no claim, no worktree, no status change, same report.
- [ ] **AC4 — Drive parity.** `phase_drive()` spawns no child session for a guarded child and surfaces `guarded_children` (plus an explicit "guarded by `do-not-delegate`" message) rather than a misleading "blocked or held" stop.
- [ ] **AC5 — Explicit override unchanged.** Direct `implement.py start <child>`, `finish <child>` and `drive <child>` on a guarded item continue to work — only automatic selection inside parent recursion is gated.
- [ ] **AC6 — Regression tests.** Tests cover the classifier (guarded / unguarded / case-and-whitespace variants / missing tags), a mixed parent set (guarded child with the lowest `sortIndex` plus open siblings → sibling starts, guarded reported), an all-guarded parent (no advance, guarded message, idempotent re-run), and `drive` (no session spawned). Tests fail before the change and pass after.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation updated.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` guard list documents the `do-not-delegate` skip, and the affected docstrings (`_classify_child`, `_next_child_to_implement`, `phase_parent`, `phase_drive`) plus any `docs/dev/` reference describe the new action and report field.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Automatic selection only.** `do-not-delegate` guards parent recursion; naming the child explicitly is the documented override (mirrors `wl delegate --force`).
- **Guarded ≠ terminal.** A guarded child must never count toward parent advancement.
- **Do not widen scope** to the stale-worktree-branch half of the superset item (its AC3/AC4) — that is a separate fix.
- **No new subprocess per child:** rely on the `tags` already present in `wl show --children` output.
- **Additive report shape:** existing fields (`children_processed`, `blocked_children`, `next_child`) keep their meaning; `guarded_children` is new.
- **No behaviour change** for terminal, in-progress or dependency-blocked classifications, and no change to the deterministic topological ordering.
- Changes affect every project once `scripts/install_pi.sh` is re-run, so the change must be built, tested and shipped on `dev` before installation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — add a `DO_NOT_DELEGATE_TAG` constant and tag helper, a `skip-do-not-delegate` branch in `_classify_child()`, skip-and-report handling in the `phase_parent()` child loop, a `guarded_children` report field plus its waiting message, and `phase_drive()` passthrough; update affected docstrings.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_parent_do_not_delegate.py` — new regression tests (classifier, mixed parent, all-guarded, drive no-spawn).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py` — the existing parent-recursion suite (root `tests/`, not `skill/implement/tests/`); extend with the guarded-child case if a shared fixture is the cheaper fit. Sibling suites: `tests/test_implement_parent_loop.py`, `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py`.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — "Guards (deterministic, in `phase_parent`)" list entry for the `do-not-delegate` skip.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — reference documentation of the new classification action and `guarded_children` report field.

- **Assumption:** `do-not-delegate` means "no unattended agent may pick this up", matching `wl`'s own delegate guard rail; the tag is already used with that meaning in this store.

- **Risk (silent stall):** skipping a guarded child without an explicit stop reason would look like the "all children held" case; the distinct message plus `guarded_children` is the mitigation.
- **Risk (ordering regression):** the topological sort and `sortIndex` tie-breaks must be untouched — only classification changes.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the stale-worktree-branch defect in SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G and the readiness-ordering defect in SA-0MVO6UL70000HT0J are separable; any extra improvement spotted here is recorded as a follow-up item, not folded into this change.

# Run mutation testing on top-churn modules to measure real test value

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis measures how test code evolves (rewrite ratio, growth, stability), but not whether those tests **detect faults**. The largest suites are also the most mock-heavy, so a high line count and long survival could reflect tests that exercise mocks rather than behaviour. Until we measure fault detection directly, conclusions about TDD return on investment rest on a proxy. Mutation testing injects small faults into source code and checks whether the suite fails; the mutation score turns "big suite" into "does this suite earn its runtime".

## Users

- **Producer / engineering manager** — wants per-module mutation scores to validate or falsify TDD-ROI claims.
- **Maintainer of the agent infrastructure** — wants a pinned, reproducible campaign that can be rerun and compared over time.
- **Agent implementing testing-policy work** — wants one documented command and machine-readable output.

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I want a mutation-score table for the top-churn suites so I can see whether their size reflects real fault detection.
- As the infrastructure maintainer, I want the tool pinned and the command documented so a rerun is comparable.
- As an agent, I want the results in JSON so the test-value aggregator can consume them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A mutation-testing tool is selected and documented — **Stryker Mutator with the vitest runner** is the working choice — with rationale, licence (Apache-2.0) and version pinned in a lockfile.
- [ ] AC2: The campaign runs against the **source modules primarily exercised by the top three churn test suites**, with a documented suite→source mapping, and reports a mutation score per module and overall.
- [ ] AC3: Results are joined with each suite's size and mock density, and the hypothesis ("high-volume, mock-heavy suites detect fewer faults") is explicitly tested rather than asserted.
- [ ] AC4: Findings are written up and appended to the TDD-value assessment with explicit caveats: sampling/scoping, equivalent mutants, mutants killed for brittle internal-coupling reasons, and runtime cost.
- [ ] AC5: The campaign is reproducible — pinned tool version, documented command, deterministic config, and automated tests for the wrapper/report parsing — and does not regress the target project's test suite.
- [ ] AC6: Runtime cost is measured and bounded (proposed bound: ≤15 min per module, ≤45 min per scoped run) so the campaign can be run periodically; the bound and cadence are documented.
- [ ] AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the target repository; no source changes to the analysed project.
- Scoped mutation, not whole-repo: `worklist.ts` is 5,944 lines and must be limited to functions its tests actually exercise.
- Mutation tooling is not part of the target project's normal CI test suite (runtime cost).
- No hardcoded project paths; the target root is an argument and is resolved like `skill/test-churn`.
- Equivalent mutants and sampling are documented limitations, not silently ignored.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is owned by the ship release pipeline and is not hand-edited here.
- Follow the repository skill contract and `$(skill_path ...)` shared-library resolution.

## Existing state

- `skill/test-churn` already produces the top-churn input. Analysis of `ContextHub` ranks these test files highest: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (101 commits), `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (84), `tests/database.test.ts` (72).
- Source mapping verified by imports:
  - `downtime-worker.test.ts` → `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (239 lines).
  - `worklist.test.ts` → `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (5,944 lines).
  - `database.test.ts` → `src/database.ts` (93-line re-export wrapper) plus the real implementation `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (2,083 lines).
- `ContextHub` uses `vitest`; neither it nor SorraAgents has Stryker installed today.
- Static anti-pattern detection exists in `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` plus `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`; it is a cheap pre-filter, not behavioural evidence.
- Epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` names mutation testing as its evidence/tie-break arm.

## Desired change

- Add `skill/mutation-test/` with a pinned Stryker config, a wrapper that resolves the target root, scopes mutation, invokes Stryker and parses its JSON report, and tests for both.
- Run the campaign against the `ContextHub` top-three modules and record per-module scores, mutant counts and runtime.
- Join the scores with churn size and mock density and write the interpretation, including the explicit hypothesis verdict and caveats.
- Document the periodic command, the runtime bound and the scoping rules.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/mutation-test/SKILL.md` — Skill contract: purpose, when-to-use, workflow, outputs, limitations.
- `skill/mutation-test/stryker.conf.json` — Pinned Stryker/vitest-runner config and mutation scope.
- `skill/mutation-test/scripts/run_mutation.py` — Resolve target root, build/merge config, invoke Stryker, parse the JSON report.
- `skill/mutation-test/scripts/suite_source_map.json` — Documented top-churn suite→source mapping (per project).
- `skill/mutation-test/tests/test_run_mutation.py` — Wrapper and config-merge tests (no real Stryker run).
- `skill/mutation-test/tests/test_report_parsing.py` — Report parsing and score arithmetic tests.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — Install/symlink the new skill.
- `docs/dev/mutation-testing.md` — Method, caveats, runtime bound and periodic-run instructions.
- Generated artefacts: `mutation_testing_report.md` and `mutation_report.json` in the chosen output directory.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — *Complete test-value refactor: ensure every test earns its runtime* (epic; mutation testing is its evidence arm).
- `SA-0MV28WNFY009DF6Y` — *Migrate test-churn / TDD-value analysis to SorraAgents and make reporting reproducible* (completed; provides the top-churn input).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — *Prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators* (explains brittle kills).
- `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU` — *scheduled test-churn runs across projects* (cadence precedent).
- `SA-0MVXVBZT7003VOCO` — test-value aggregator (consumer of mutation results).
- `SA-0MVXVC33N007Q71K` — assertion-quality / mock-density analyser (supplies the mock-density independent variable).
- `SA-0MVXVC6C4009661D` — near-duplicate test detection (complementary cheap signal).
- `SA-0MVXVC9FM003ZJKJ` — per-test runtime and flakiness (cost side of the value ratio).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** broader runtime budgets, more modules, or other languages must be filed as linked work items, not pulled into this item.
- **Runtime risk:** `worklist.ts` is very large; without function-level scoping the campaign will exceed any reasonable budget. Scoping rules are part of the deliverable.
- **Equivalent-mutant risk:** some survivors cannot be killed. The report must caveat this and sample-review survivors rather than treating every survivor as weak coverage.
- **Brittle-kill risk:** a mutant can be killed because a test asserts an internal collaborator call, not observable behaviour. Record this separately using the assertion-quality signal.
- **Assumption (Q1):** the campaign lives in a reusable `skill/mutation-test/` in SorraAgents, not a ContextHub-local script, because AC5 requires a pinned reproducible command and SorraAgents is the canonical skills home.
- **Assumption (Q2):** mutate the source modules primarily exercised by the top-three churn suites, using the documented suite→source mapping above; this directly tests AC3's hypothesis.
- **Assumption (Q3):** the runtime bound is ≤15 min per module and ≤45 min per scoped run, with a weekly/per-release cadence; the producer may override this.
- **Assumption:** the target project remains `ContextHub` (TypeScript/vitest). If the producer prefers SorraAgents' Python suite, `mutmut` would be the tool and the scoring model would need re-checking.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should the mutation-testing campaign live?" — **OPEN QUESTION (assumed for this brief):** a reusable `skill/mutation-test/` in SorraAgents (option a). Rationale: AC5 requires a pinned, reproducible command; SorraAgents is the canonical skills home; a ContextHub-local script would duplicate infrastructure. Source: repo evidence (`skill/test-churn`, `scripts/install_pi.sh`) and the seed's AC5.
- Q2: "Which source modules should be mutated?" — **OPEN QUESTION (assumed for this brief):** the source modules primarily exercised by the top-three churn suites (option a), with the suite→source mapping recorded. Rationale: directly tests AC3's hypothesis and keeps the churn evidence as the sampling frame. Evidence: imports inspected in `ContextHub`.

## Goal

As an operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`, I want the CPU / memory / I/O stall pressure metrics to report real values, so the diagnosis is based on the kernel's own pressure-stall signal instead of silently losing three of its twelve metrics.

## Problem statement

`skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/metrics.py::_read_proc_pressure()` never matches a PSI line, so `cpu_pressure`, `memory_pressure` and `io_pressure` are permanently rendered `n/a` ("unavailable (non-Linux or kernel missing pressure stall info)") even when `/proc/pressure/*` is present and readable — three of the twelve before-table metrics are dead weight and the pressure analysis in Step 2 can never fire on stall data.

## Users

- **Operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`** — "As an operator, I want the before table to show the kernel's stall percentages so I can tell CPU contention from memory or I/O starvation without guessing."
- **Agent triaging a slow host** — "As an agent, I want the numeric pressure value in the metrics dict so `pressure_analysis.analyze_pressures()` can surface a real pressure with contributors instead of skipping the metric."
- **Skill maintainer** — "As a maintainer, I want PSI parsing covered by verbatim-content unit tests so a wrong fixture can't mask the bug again."

## Evidence (verified)

Re-verified on this host (16-core Ubuntu, 2026-10-23): all three collectors return `None` while PSI is readable.

```
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=84206005618   # /proc/pressure/cpu
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=64384303      # /proc/pressure/memory (some)
full avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=35437059      # /proc/pressure/memory (full)
some avg10=0.05 avg60=0.11 avg300=0.10 total=398915844     # /proc/pressure/io (some)
full avg10=0.05 avg60=0.11 avg300=0.10 total=270870893     # /proc/pressure/io (full)
```

Original discovery run (2026-10-21) showed genuine CPU `some` pressure of `avg10=11.58` alongside load 11.92 on 16 cores — real signal was thrown away.

## Root cause

```python
for line in lines:
    if line.startswith("avg"):        # never true — lines start with "some " / "full "
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 4:
            return float(parts[1])    # tokens are avg10=<v> etc., not bare numbers
return None
```

Two independent defects: the prefix test can never match, and the value token needs `split("=")` (not whitespace index 1). The existing unit test passes only because it feeds a fabricated two-line fixture (`some:stuff` followed by `avg10  60.00 60.00 60.00`) that matches the buggy parser rather than real kernel output.

## Desired change

1. `_read_proc_pressure(key: str, which: str = "some") -> float | None` parses real PSI output, returning the `avg10` stall percentage of the requested `some`/`full` line; returns `None` when the file is missing/empty/unparsable or the requested line is absent.
2. `pressure_specs` gains a per-metric line selector (decided: **`cpu` → `some`; `memory` → `full`; `io` → `full`**) so the semantic choice is explicit in code.
3. Each metric's `description` names the line used and its basis, e.g. `"CPU stall pressure (some avg10, % of time any task stalled)"`, so the table is self-documenting; the `n/a` description states which line was requested.
4. `memory_pressure` gets its **own** `config.yaml` block (and `config.py::_DEFAULTS` entry) calibrated for `full`-line semantics — `warning: 5`, `critical: 20` — replacing the current accidental mapping to `memory_usage` 80/95.
5. `SKILL.md` metric table gains a line-selection column and documents the `some` vs `full` semantics, the new `memory_pressure` block, and the no-fallback degradation rule.

## Implementation plan (test-first, single vertical slice)

**Decomposition decision: no child work items.** The change is one Small, self-contained vertical slice (parser → wiring → config → docs → tests) confined to a single skill; splitting it would add coordination overhead without reducing risk. Test-first ordering is expressed as the sequence below and enforced by the build → test → commit gate during implementation.

1. **Failing parser tests first** (`tests/test_metrics.py::TestReadProcPressure`) — delete the fabricated `avg10  60.00 …` fixture, add verbatim kernel samples (cpu `some`-only; memory/io `some` + `full`), asserting the expected `avg10` values and that `which="some"` vs `which="full"` select different lines of the same sample — **AC1**. Verify: new tests fail (RED) against today's `_read_proc_pressure`.
2. **Failure-mode tests** — missing file, present-but-unparsable (`avg10=abc`), requested `full` line absent (documented no-fallback), empty file → `None` — **AC2**.
3. **Parser implementation** (`scripts/metrics.py::_read_proc_pressure(key, which="some")`) — select the `some ` / `full ` line, parse `avg10=<v>` with `split("=")`, return `float`, `None` on any failure — **AC1, AC2**. Verify: steps 1–2 tests GREEN.
4. **Config block** (`scripts/config.py::_DEFAULTS` + `config.yaml`) — add `memory_pressure` (`low: 0`, `warning: 5`, `critical: 20`) calibrated for `full`-line semantics; fix the misleading "Memory Pressure" heading above `memory_usage`; `tests/test_config.py` gains defaults + file-override assertions — **AC5**.
5. **Wiring + description tests** (`collect_metrics`) — `pressure_specs` gains a per-metric line selector (`cpu`→`some`, `memory`→`full`, `io`→`full`) and `memory_pressure` resolves to the new config key; descriptions carry line + basis (e.g. `"CPU stall pressure (some avg10, % of time any task stalled)"`) and the `n/a` description names the requested line; a mocked-PSI test asserts rendered values, statuses and descriptions — **AC3, AC6**.

# Pinned suiteCommands precedence and no-double-execution

## Goal

Implement D3 of SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB for the pinned/uncovered and
double-execution cases: a project's pinned `.pi/test-config.json`
`suiteCommands` list is returned verbatim (nothing appended) while a
machine-readable, non-fatal notice names the hidden skill test dirs the
pinned list does not cover; a candidate already collected via the project's
pytest `testpaths`/`addopts` is skipped.

## Design decisions (elaborating D3; recorded in the parent's Appendix)

- **Notice surface.** A new pure accessor `hidden_skill_test_notice(root)` (or
  `full_suite_notices(root)`) returns a machine-readable structure naming the
  uncovered directories plus a stable code (`hidden_skill_tests_uncovered`).
  `full_suite_commands()` keeps its `list[str]` signature (D4 — no consumer
  sees a signature change). `run_tests.py` surfaces the notice non-fatally:
  in `--json` output under `resolution_notices` and as a single stderr
  warning line when resolving a full suite whose `suiteCommands` is pinned.
  Exit status unchanged.
- **Skip rule (no double execution).** A candidate is "already covered" when
  a token in the project's pytest `testpaths` (INI `[pytest]` or
  `pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` form) or an `addopts` path
  token resolves to `.pi` or a strict descendant of `.pi` AND the candidate
  is a descendant-or-equal of that token (normalised, repo-relative). Tokens
  at or above the repo root (`.`, `tests`, `skill`) do NOT count as
  covering: default `norecursedirs` pruning still prevents `.pi` collection
  from those roots, so treating them as coverage would silently re-silence
  the hidden tests D1 exists to surface. Custom `norecursedirs`/`--ignore`
  overrides are out of scope (documented as such).

## Acceptance Criteria (parent AC3 + AC4)

- **AC3 — Pinned `suiteCommands` precedence proven.** A repo with
  `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` gets its list back verbatim (no
  append) AND `hidden_skill_test_notice()` names the uncovered hidden skill
  test dirs with a stable machine-readable code; one regression test pins
  both behaviours. An explicitly-empty pinned list is also returned verbatim
  with a notice.
- **AC4 — No double execution.** A candidate already covered by the project's
  pytest `testpaths`/`addopts` (INI and pyproject forms) is skipped: in the
  INI form the same candidate "covered" only by a token at repo root or
  above (`.`, `tests`) is still emitted; a candidate fully absent from
  config is emitted. Tests cover the INI and pyproject forms plus the
  uncovered case.
- **AC4b — Notice is non-fatal.** Resolution result and process exit status
  are unchanged whether or not a notice is present.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — notice accessor + skip-rule helper;
  `extension_suite_commands()`/`_read_test_config` readers (precedence
  inputs), `full_suite_commands()`
- `skill/test/tests/test_hidden_skill_tests.py` — AC3/AC4 tests
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` notice plumbing conventions referenced
  from `NOTICE_*` constants (non-fatal by construction)

# implement.py finish deletes a plain leaf session's cwd, breaking its post-finish steps

`discovered-from:SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR` — split out of the driven-session worktree-removal fix at producer request (Q2 of that item's intake). Same root cause, different caller: here the *session that invoked finish* is the operator's own agent session, not a driver-spawned child.

**Headline:** `implement.py finish` must not leave a plain leaf session unable to run any command: after finish removes the worktree, Pi's bash tool refuses every call in that session, so the report, the worklog comment and the post-push verification steps all fail.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` removes the worktree after the dev push (Step 7, `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:5322`). In the plain leaf flow the finishing process is a **child** of the agent session (`bash` tool), and that session's cwd *is* the worktree. `_remove_worktree` chdirs only the finish process out of the tree (`:2364-2376`), so the session keeps a deleted cwd: Pi's bash tool then rejects every command with `Working directory does not exist: … / Cannot execute bash commands.` while absolute-path `read`/`write` still work. The session is reduced to a degraded loop exactly when it should be writing its completion comment, rendering its report and verifying the pushed commit.

## Users and user stories

- **Implement agent (plain leaf item)** — "As an agent finishing a leaf work item, I want my post-finish steps to run normally, so I do not have to invent absolute-path workarounds for the report and the post-push verification."
- **Operator / reviewer** — "As the reviewer, I want the session's final report and verification evidence produced by the workflow rather than improvised, so I can trust what I read."
- **Maintainer** — "As the maintainer, I want one deterministic rule for when a worktree may be deleted relative to the session that owns it."

## Recorded evidence

- **RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33** (session `01a1840b-13a6-71a0-9153-f89e8dd2dfee`, TCE repo): the session hit `Working directory does not exist` **8 times** after its foreground `implement.py finish`, then worked around it — its own transcript notes "After that bash won't work, so do it last", and it removed a placeholder directory as its final action.
- Same failure mode documented in `SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR` for driven sessions (where it also wedges the drive loop); that item fixes the driven case only.

## Desired change (direction, not a fixed design)

The driven case is solved by deferring removal to the driver. The plain case has no external owner, so the options are:

1. **Defer to the session's own last step** — finish keeps the worktree and the implement skill's finish step ends with an explicit, runnable cleanup instruction (`git worktree remove … && git worktree prune`) that the *session* performs as its final action, after the comment, report and verification are done.
2. **Defer to a separate cleanup pass** — finish always defers; the cleanup skill / `implement.py` gains a `cleanup` action that removes worktrees of terminal items, run by the operator or the next workflow step.
3. **Make finish's removal non-fatal to the session** — keep removing, but ensure nothing after it needs bash (move report rendering/comment/verification *before* removal inside finish). Cheapest, but leaves the session's cwd dead for any later operator-driven interaction.

A design decision is required at intake/plan time; option 1 or 2 is expected to fit the existing `--keep-worktree` hatch added by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — No dead cwd after finish in the plain flow.** A plain leaf session can still run bash commands after `implement.py finish` returns (or the workflow guarantees nothing after finish needs bash — depending on the chosen option), verified by a test that drives `phase_finish` and asserts the session-visible worktree state.
- [ ] **AC2 — Cleanup still happens deterministically.** Whichever option is chosen, a finished leaf item's worktree is removed by a named step within the same workflow run (session final action or cleanup pass), with the removal recorded in the finish/cleanup report.
- [ ] **AC3 — Consistency with the driven fix.** The mechanism reuses the deferral predicate/flag introduced by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR (`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE`, `--keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE`) rather than adding a third removal path.
- [ ] **AC4 — Interruption safety.** An interrupted workflow leaves the worktree present and reported (never half-removed), and a repeat run is idempotent.
- [ ] **AC5 — Documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (finish step cleanup instructions), `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` state the ownership rule for the plain flow.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation criterion.** New tests plus the changed-scope suite pass via the test skill (`/skill:test`), and the dev-push full-suite gate is green for the pushed commit.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do **not** change the driven-session behaviour delivered by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR; this item is the non-driven path only.
- Reuse `_remove_worktree`, `cleanup_worktree_processes` and the existing safety gates; no new deletion mechanism, no `rm -rf`-style shortcuts.
- Never remove a worktree that is dirty or whose item is non-terminal.
- Pi core's bash-tool behaviour on a missing cwd is out of scope (a Pi-core limitation, not fixable here).
- **Out of scope:** the pane transport, `hygiene_check.sh` rework, branch deletion.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 6b/7 and the finish-step ordering, plus the deferral predicate shared with SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — finish-step cleanup instructions (currently a manual `git worktree remove` block, `SKILL.md:811`).
- `skill/implement/tests/` — extend the finish test harness (`test_finish_no_diff_status.py` style) for the plain-flow behaviour.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — ownership rule for the plain flow.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR** — "implement.py finish removes the worktree under a driven child session, wedging it" (open, parent of this split): fixes the driven path; this item must reuse its deferral mechanism.
- **SA-0MVJC5KNT0044L2B** — finish SIGTERMing itself in `wl cleanup-worktree` (completed): the self-exclusion contract around Step 6b.
- **SA-0MRTSO5W8005ZGA7** — added the worktree process cleanup call to the workflow (completed).
- **RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33** — the plain-flow session that hit the deleted cwd 8 times (completed).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Options 1/2 leave worktrees behind on interruption** — mitigated by AC4 and by the cleanup skill.
- **Doc/instruction drift:** `SKILL.md` currently instructs the agent to run `git worktree remove` itself after pushing, duplicating finish's removal; the chosen option must make the instruction and the code agree.
- **Assumption:** the operator's session is the only other holder of the worktree cwd in the plain flow (no other process needs it), so removal timing is purely about the session's own remaining steps.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "just make Pi tolerate a deleted cwd" is a Pi-core change — record it, do not attempt it here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Scope split.** *Answer (producer, during SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR intake): "driver only, raise a follow up item for the plain leaf flow".* This item is that follow-up; the driven path is SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR.
- **Q2 (OPEN QUESTION, for planning) — Which cleanup owner for the plain flow?** (1) the session's own final step, (2) a separate cleanup pass, (3) move everything that needs bash before removal inside finish. Recommended: **(1)**, because it keeps a single workflow run responsible for its own cleanup and reuses the `--keep-worktree` hatch; (2) becomes preferable if the cleanup skill is the operator's normal sweep.
- **Q3 (answered by research) — Is the failure a hang?** No: bash is refused for the rest of the session while absolute-path file tools still work; the session degrades but does not block (RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33's workaround).

# Intake Brief — long-lived branches whose upstream is `.` silently break `git pull`

**Priority: critical. Issue type: bug.**

## Summary

On a worktree-heavy machine, `dev` (or `main`) can end up with
`branch.<name>.remote = .`. Plain `git pull` then resolves the upstream to the
**same repository**, prints `From .` / `Already up to date`, exits 0, and no
remote data ever arrives. Every agent on that machine keeps running stale
skills/runner code while believing it is up to date, with no warning anywhere.

Observed live on 2026-10-31 (rgardler-AI-Laptop): the machine stayed on
`b50ccedc` for hours after `a2659c38` landed (the test-runner fix that removes
the 2-slot starvation), so it kept queueing every test run behind a 2-slot pool
while `origin` held the fixed runner. `origin` was configured correctly and
`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev` showed the true tip — only the
**branch-level** tracking key was wrong, and that is the key `git pull` reads.

## Evidence

```
$ git pull
From .
 * branch                dev        -> FETCH_HEAD
Already up to date.

$ git log --oneline -1
b50ccedc SA-0MVQHVKUH009VQMD: Implementation complete        # stale

$ git config --get branch.dev.remote
.
$ git config --get branch.dev.merge
refs/heads/dev

$ git remote -v
origin  git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/SorraAgents.git (fetch)   # correct
$ git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev
a2659c38f075d367668df5c3ffa48bcc8aeb75cb                     # true tip
```

Desktop counterpart, the healthy shape — long-lived branches point at `origin`,
only `wl-*` worktree branches use `.`:

```
[branch "main"]                                              remote = origin
[branch "dev"]                                               remote = origin
[branch "wl-SA-0MQSFWFB1007R2I7-extract-level-from-score"]   remote = .
[branch "wl-SA-0MSN6FBFS006Z5QP-implement-run-tests-canonical"] remote = .
...                                                          (all wl-* = .)
```

## Mechanism (reproduced in a scratch repo, not inferred)

`branch.<name>.remote` is **one key per branch name**, stored in the shared
`.git/config` that all worktrees use. Two supported operations write `.` into
it:

```bash
# 1. Worktree registration tracking a LOCAL base branch — implement.py:2339
git worktree add --track -b wl-<id>-<slug> <path> dev
  → branch.wl-<id>-<slug>.remote = .
    branch.wl-<id>-<slug>.merge  = refs/heads/dev

# 2. A push whose remote is the local path form
git push -u . dev:dev
  → branch 'dev' set up to track './dev'.
    branch.dev.remote = .
    branch.dev.merge  = refs/heads/dev

# (git branch --track dev dev / --set-upstream-to=dev dev refuse:
#  "not setting branch 'dev' as its own upstream", "--track needs a new branch")
```

For a `wl-*` branch `.` is the correct, intentional *worktree-ownership* signal
(`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py:595-608`, `live_repo_guard.py:29`) and it
**survives `git worktree remove`** — that survival is already load-bearing for
sandbox cleanup. On `dev`/`main` the identical value silently disables
`git pull` for the whole machine.

Why a fix, not just a guard: the write path is still live. As long as any tool
or operator can push with a path-form remote (`.`) or register a worktree on a
long-lived branch, a fresh clone can re-acquire the defect, and the failure mode
is silent success.

## Blast radius

- **Stale agent infrastructure.** Skills are symlinked into the checkout
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills -> <repo>/skill`), so a no-op pull means agents on that
  machine run old runner/gate/audit logic indefinitely. This already cost hours
  of queueing (the 2-slot `test` pool) after the fix had merged.
- **Stale worklog data.** `refs/worklog/data` is fetched on pull; a no-op pull
  means the machine's `wl` view diverges (stale statuses, missing items), and
  `wl sync` may then push a stale merge base.
- **Silent, so it compounds.** `git pull` exits 0, so scripts, agent sessions and
  the operator all conclude "up to date".
- Affects **both** repos on a machine (SorraAgents and llm-manager), plus any
  other worktree-managed checkout.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Detect.** A check reports every local branch whose tracking config resolves
   to itself — `branch.<name>.remote == "."` **or** `branch.<name>.merge`
   pointing at that same branch — and classifies it: **defect** for long-lived
   branches (`dev`, `main`, and any branch named in the repo's release config),
   **expected** for `wl-*` worktree branches, which must never be reported.
2. **Repair, machine-readable and safe.** One command (or `--fix`) repairs a
   defect to `remote=origin` / `merge=refs/heads/<branch>` **only** when
   `origin` is a real remote whose `refs/heads/<branch>` exists, otherwise it
   refuses with an actionable message (never guess a remote, never rewrite a
   `wl-*` branch, never touch `main`/`dev` working trees).
3. **Prevent — write path closed.** No framework code path can produce
   `remote=.` for a long-lived branch:
   - `implement.py` worktree creation keeps `--track` for the `wl-*` branch (the
     ownership signal is required) but asserts afterwards that the **parent**
     branch's tracking config is untouched, and fails loudly if a worktree
     registration ever writes `remote=.` onto the parent branch name;
   - any framework `git push` uses the configured remote **name** (`origin`),
     never a path/`.` form, so `-u` can never record a self-upstream;
   - a regression test proves both properties.
4. **Prevent — detection runs where it matters.** The check is wired into
   `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` (so the periodic/CI run reports it) and surfaced
   by `implement.py start` as a **warning** (fail-open: it must never block a
   work item, and must never rewrite config implicitly).
5. **Verification on a real machine.** After repair, `git pull` fetches from
   `origin` (not `.`), `git log origin/dev..dev` is empty, and the installed
   runner reports the current values (e.g.
   `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT=6`, `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST_DEFAULT=4`,
   `TEST_FAST_SEMAPHORE_NAME=test-fast`) — recorded as evidence on this item.
6. **Docs.** A short section in the worktree-isolation / git-hooks docs stating
   that `branch.<name>.remote` is shared per **branch name** across worktrees,
   that `.` is the legitimate worktree-ownership signal which survives
   `git worktree remove`, and that `.` on a long-lived branch makes `git pull`
   a silent no-op.
7. **Deterministic tests** (no network): scratch-repo fixtures for
   `worktree add --track -b X <path> dev` (X gets `.`, `dev` unchanged),
   `git push -u . dev:dev` (detected as a defect on `dev`), a self-referential
   `merge`, a healthy `origin`-tracked branch (no finding), and a `wl-*`
   branch with `.` (no finding).

## Out of scope

- Changing git's own semantics or rewriting `.` tracking for existing `wl-*`
  branches (required by sandbox cleanup).
- Auto-repairing machines without operator intent (the fix must be explicit;
  only detection is automatic).

## Affected machines / rollout

- `rgardler-AI-Laptop`: `dev` upstream is `.` in **both** SorraAgents and
  llm-manager — repair with
  `git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/dev dev`, then re-verify the runner and
  the stall-guard commit (`llm-manager` `dev` = `3b9c57f5`).
- Desktop (`sorra-agents-1`): verified healthy (`dev`/`main` = `origin`); no

Record a `refactor` verify entry **report-only** — a violation found there is surfaced in the report and in a wl comment but does not abort, preserving today's non-gating refactor semantics. ## Goal

As a producer/agent, I want a single, reproducible per-test-file **keep / rework / prune** verdict that combines churn, mutation, anti-pattern and runtime evidence, so test-value decisions are made from one reconciled report rather than four separate reads.

## Problem statement

Today the evidence for test value is fragmented across `skill/test-churn` (evolution/growth), the mutation-testing campaign (`SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`, fault detection), `evaluate_usefulness.py` + `test-writing-guidelines.md` (static anti-patterns) and the test runner (runtime/flake). Each answers a different question; none produces an auditable per-file verdict. Epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` needs a repeatable classify → prove → report pipeline, and this skill is the missing connective tissue between those signals.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ingests, per test file: churn metrics (rewrite/growth/stability), mutation score, anti-pattern verdicts, and runtime/flake data when available.
- [ ] Emits one verdict per file — `keep`, `rework` or `prune` — with the evidence for that verdict recorded.
- [ ] Totals reconcile: verdict counts sum to files in scope, and every verdict cites at least one evidence source.
- [ ] Produces `test_value_report.md` + `test_value_data.json` with documented definitions and limitations.
- [ ] Orchestrates the existing analysers; it does not reimplement churn, mutation or anti-pattern detection.
- [ ] Missing inputs degrade honestly (the report states which signals were absent; it never fabricates a verdict).
- [ ] Reproducible (pinned inputs, documented command, deterministic ordering) and covered by tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the analysed project.
- Must not turn a heuristic into an automatic deletion; `prune` is advisory and conservative.

- Follows the repository skill contract and `$(skill_path ...)` shared-library resolution.

Keep the existing stale-state rejection, and keep the current fallback (stated root, or cwd discovery) only when derivation is impossible (`_get_repo_root` returns `None`), with a warning. ## Goal

As a test-value reviewer, I want a cheap static measure of how a test asserts and how much it relies on mocks, so I can pre-filter the suites that mutation testing should examine and give `toHaveBeenCalledWith`-style coupling an enforceable signal.

## Problem statement

`evaluate_usefulness.py` detects only crude anti-patterns (source-grep, placeholder, zero assertions, self-referential). It cannot distinguish a test that asserts observable behaviour from one that asserts internal collaborator calls, nor quantify mock density — yet mock density is a central independent variable in the hypothesis that high-volume mock-heavy suites detect fewer faults. ## Goal

As a producer, I want per-test runtime and flake history so I can express test value as fault detection per second of suite runtime and bound the cost of periodic mutation campaigns.

## Problem statement

Test value is currently measured without its cost. The test runner reports suite-level timing, but there is no per-test timing or flake history, so a valuable-but-slow test and a worthless-but-slow test are indistinguishable, and mutation-campaign runtime cannot be allocated sensibly. The test-value epic (`SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`, AC7) also needs before/after runtime evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The test runner records per-test duration and a bounded flake history across runs.
- [ ] Emits a machine-readable report consumable by the test-value aggregator (churn/mutation/runtime join).
- [ ] Overhead is bounded and documented; normal runs stay within the existing runtime budget.
- [ ] Flake detection is deterministic for repeated failures and does not hide genuine failures.
- [ ] Integrated into the existing `skill/test` runner rather than a new measurement skill.
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Must not change the pass/fail semantics of the test runner.
- History storage is bounded (retention policy documented).
- Follows the test-execution policy: agents still invoke tests only via the test skill; infrastructure gates are out of scope.
